limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Use line-level profiling to reduce exposed Python request-preparation, scheduling and execution-coordination overhead in a bounded serving optimization loop.
applicability.prerequisites: Confirm host overhead is the limiting factor with the detection procedure before tuning; choose a representative workload and consistent CPU affinity for comparisons.
applicability.input_contract: Detection/NVTX triage, qualified target function paths and line-profiler output, workload/affinity settings, related correctness tests and serving benchmark metrics.
applicability.produced_artifact: Per-round hotspot/change/rollback and correctness records plus a final before/after benchmark report, failed attempts, remaining hotspots and scoped follow-up recommendations.
applicability.failure_modes: Optimizing the default preparation function can miss a different regressing owner; caching/hoisting/preallocation can violate lifetime or invalidation, and a line-level speedup can leave serving throughput unchanged.

recommendations: Profile the actual top regressing function by absolute exposed time, drilling into dominant unprofiled subcalls instead of assuming _prepare_tp_inputs is the owner.
Prefer one small evidence-supported change with explicit ownership/lifetime/invalidation checks, run relevant correctness tests and revert failed or regressing candidates.
Re-profile identical workloads after each accepted change and compare hotspot time, total function time and serving metrics; reassess the next bottleneck and stay within the authorized budget.
